title: Unit 1 – The Ayeyarwady Dolphins
content:
A: Hi! Kyaw Swar, you've just come back from Chaung Tha, haven't you?
B: Yes, I have.
A: (1) How was your trip?
B: Fantastic! I got a lot of experience from it.
A: Did you? (2) With whom did you go there?
B: I went there with a voluntary group to do the project on the environment.
A: (3) What did you do with that group?
B: When we arrived there, we collected litter on the beach and buried the garbage bags in the hole that we dug away from the beach.
A: What a good deed! (4) What did you do after that?
B: When I came back to the beach, I saw a sea turtle crawling on the sand. So my friend and I carried it and released it into the sea.
A: (5) How did you feel after the trip?
B: Well, I was pleased for what I had done in Chaung Tha. I hope you can join us when we go on the next trip.

title: Unit 2 – Online Shopping
content:
Dialogue 1
A: Hi! Bo Bo, what do you do on the net?
B: I use the internet mainly (1) for banking.
A: Why?
B: (2) It's good because I can check my balance anytime. I can transfer money, too. I like paying bills online. It's very convenient.
A: Is it difficult to pay bills online?
B: Of course not. You just log on your bank and click on (3) "Pay now", and the bill is paid immediately.
A: Hey! Yi Phyo! What do you do on the net?
B: I do my weekly shopping, and (4) things are all delivered.
A: What do you usually buy?
B: Clothes, birthday presents, Christmas presents, books, music – the lot!
A: Wow! (5) Which website do you usually use?
B: Ah, a variety of websites. But my favorite is Shop.com.

Dialogue 2
A: What do you do on the net?
B: I use the net to look for jobs and flats, and to see what's on. I also use the net (1) for Facebook.
A: Wow! What can we do on Facebook?
B: (2) You can find new friends especially when you identify someone you'd like to meet on the site. We normally share common interests. It's really exciting.
A: What do you do on the net?
B: (3) I do my weekly shopping and things are all delivered.
A: What do you usually buy?
B: Clothes, birthday presents, Christmas presents, books, music – (4) the lot!
A: Wow! Which website do you usually use?
B: Ah, a variety of websites. But (5) my favorite is Shop.com.

title: Unit 3 – Memory
content:
Lin Lin: We should have a time to relax after the exam. What do you think?
Thiri: I think (1) I agree with you. How about going shopping to the City Mall? We can have a lot of fun there.
Lin Lin: (2) I don't think so. There's a lot of people and it is a bit noisy. I wish to go to a quiet place.
Thiri: (3) You're right but we can have good food at the Food Court and can also watch a movie if you like. You like watching movies, don't you? It's relaxing to watch a comedy.
Lin Lin: OK. (4) I see your point now. Let's watch a movie after having lunch.

title: Unit 7 – Systems and Organs of the Human Body
content:
Thinzar: Hi, Su Mon. We haven't seen each other since the beginning of the Thadingyut holiday. (1) What have you been doing?
Su Mon: I went on a trip to Bagan with my cousins. After the trip, I helped my mum with the housework. (2) What about you? Did you go anywhere?
Thinzar: No, I didn't. I just stayed at home, sitting in front of the TV right after meals for about four or five hours every day, and now I've put on 5 pounds! If I go on like this, I'll gain 10 pounds by the end of this month!
Su Mon: (3) If it's your real concern, why don't you take up something challenging? Many people try to reduce weight by doing workouts or doing sports. These will burn calories and make you more energetic.
Thinzar: I think it's a good idea. That will reduce my weight and I'll also have a chance to go out. (4) What sports would you recommend?
Su Mon: Well, you can take up either team sports or individual sports. Both are good for health. With team sports you can develop a sense of fair play and social skills. Some of my classmates are doing team sports like basketball, volleyball and football.
Thinzar: For me, I prefer individual sports.
Su Mon: If so, choose sports like swimming, gymnastics or kickboxing.
Thinzar: (5) I'll definitely choose swimming. It doesn't cost me much.
Su Mon: OK, then. You'd better start going swimming soon before you put on much weight.
Thinzar: Thanks for your advice.

title: Unit 8 – The Last Leaf
content:
A: Ni Mar, do you like the short story "The Last Leaf"?
B: Of course, I like the (1) characters of the story, Sue, Johnsy and Behrman.
A: What do you think the (2) theme of the story is?
B: I think it's about (3) friendship. The characters share similar passions. All of them are artists and they love art. And when Johnsy fell ill, Sue manages all her care. She also encourages her to think positively.
A: Mr. Behrman helps Johnsy (4) survive too. He takes the risk of falling ill – he paints a green leaf on the opposite wall in the heavy rain. That's why I think the theme of the story is selfless sacrifice.
B: Hmm, you're right. Sue is also willing to (5) sacrifice her wishes and time for her friend.
A: Yes, it proves that love and kindness is more valuable than expensive material possessions.
B: Ah, I agree with you.

title: Unit 9 – Stress And How to Beat It
content:
A: Hi Thaw Zin. (1) What happened to you? You look stressed.
B: Um, (2) I have some problems at school. I can't concentrate on my studies, so I never finish my assignments in time.
A: (3) If I were you, I'd take some time off to get some refreshment.
B: Oh, (4) I should have thought about that. And sometimes I feel depressed because of my bad friends. They're always teasing me – body shaming and giving me all sorts of nicknames. What should I do?
A: With such kind of friends, (5) you'd better ignore them. Just stay away from them. It's normal in life to face such problems.
B: Yes, you're right. Thanks.

title: Unit 12 – Natural Disasters
content:
Presenter: Today, I'm going to interview three people who witnessed natural disasters. Lwin Mar, tell us about the worst natural disaster you have experienced throughout your life.
Lwin Mar: Well, I'm now 22 and it happened thirteen years ago, on the 2nd of May while I was living in a small village in Bogalay Township, Ayeyarwady Delta. Cyclone Nargis hit our area. (1) We lost almost everything – our relatives, our homes and our businesses.
Presenter: Right now, I'd like to ask U Tint Lwin about his experience. Can you tell us about the moment you have been affected by (2) a natural disaster? What was the experience like?
U Tint Lwin: Last year, I returned to my home country from India. I was sent to (3) a quarantine centre as it was the time of COVID-19 pandemic. After four or five days of my arrival, I got a fever and couldn't sense any taste and smell. I was discharged from the hospital after I tested negative of Corona virus for 2 times. That one month was quite a hard time for me.
Presenter: I'm so sorry to hear that! Now, Daw Khin Maw, can you tell us about the natural disaster you have witnessed in your life? What was it like?
Daw Khin Maw: One fine afternoon in August, 2016, my family and I were going around the temples in Bagan. Suddenly, I felt movements on the ground and felt dizzy. As soon as we realized that (4) it was an earthquake, we ran out from the temple quickly. Luckily, no one in Bagan was injured but nearly 400 pagodas were damaged.
Presenter: That's a shame! Well, this is the end of our interview. Thanks for sharing (5) your experience with us. Thank you, all the listeners, for being with us.
